lines: Telling your AI "don't reveal secrets" is a hope with good phrasing.
By the time it reads that rule, it has already read the secret. Ask sideways, and it helpfully sums up the very file it was told to keep quiet.
The rule is a request. The context is a fact.
So put the door before the model. Every file says who it's for. A loader checks that against who's asking, and drops everything else before a single word reaches the model.
That's the whole fix: load context, with a role. And a file with no label? It counts as private. Hiding it by mistake costs one quick edit. Sharing it by mistake can't be undone.
Ask about a file it never got, and it just says: I don't have that. The model can't leak what it was never given.
